### Observed differences

- In the later window, activity A06 occurred in fewer traces: about 9 in 100 traces, down from about 20 in 100 traces before. Its mean occurrences per trace fell from about 0.24 to 0.10, and traces with repeated occurrences of A06 dropped from about 3 in 100 to about 1 in 100. [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. The single observed difference in activity A06's occurrence is within the range that an unchanged process could produce by chance, given that about 0.5 such items were expected and only 1 was observed. [OCC001]

Before: mean occurrences per trace 0.235, participation 0.2 (40/200 traces), recurrence support 0.03 (i.e., 3% of traces have multiple occurrences? Actually recurrence_support is proportion of traces with more than one occurrence? It says 0.03 before, 0.01 after). After: mean 0.1, participation 0.09 (18/200), recurrence 0.01. So activity A06 became less frequent: participation dropped from 20% to 9% of traces, mean occurrences per trace dropped from 0.235 to 0.1, and recurrence (traces with multiple occurrences) dropped from 3% to 1%. Observed change 0.135, empirical strength 0.995 (very high). Support: before 40 traces, after 18 traces. Screening: control_flow family: units_tested 100, items 1, expected 0.5. So one item when 0.5 expected. That is about 2 times expected, but the guidance says: "A count of the same order as that expectation (for example one or two items when fewer than one is expected) is what an unchanged process typically produces: choose 'Insufficient evidence', however large or unusual a single item looks." Here expected 0.5, items 1. That is of the same order (1 vs 0.5). So we should choose Insufficient evidence. Even though the empirical strength is high, the screening comparison says the number of items is not many times larger than expected. So we must conclude insufficient evidence. Also note that the activity A06 is not extremely frequent; support is 40 and 18 traces, which is moderate but not huge. The change is a decrease in participation and mean occurrences. But the screening says only 1 item when 0.5 expected, so it's within what an unchanged process could produce. So we should say insufficient evidence.
